frontmatter-start.comment: YAML front matter at the very start of the file. A TextMate grammar tokenizes one line at a time, so a begin pattern can never look ahead to confirm a later line is a bare +++ (the real, only rule src/mdy.js uses — see FRONT_MATTER_SEPARATOR/parseDocument). This approximates it from the one line we CAN see: front matter starts where the first line looks like a YAML `key:` mapping entry, or is +++ itself (an empty front-matter block, which parseDocument explicitly allows). A document whose body happens to open with `Word: text` is the one (rare, and not seen anywhere in this repo's own examples) case this over-triggers on.
frontmatter-start.name: meta.frontmatter.mdy

document-separator.comment: A bare --- line splits a source into multiple documents (splitDocuments). Each new document may have its own front matter, checked the same heuristic way as frontmatter-start, against the line immediately following the separator; otherwise this --- is just a plain separator and what follows is body. `end` is a zero-width lookahead for any real (non-newline) character, deliberately NOT [\s\S]: vscode-textmate appends a synthetic trailing newline to every tokenized line (so $ anchors work), and [\s\S] would match THAT, closing this region one line too early — before the nested front-matter pattern below ever gets a look at the real next line.
document-separator.name: meta.after-document-separator.mdy

escape.comment: \{{ and \{% render as literal {{ / {% (compileTemplateSource's emitLiteral unescape) — never tag delimiters.
escape.name: constant.character.escape.mdy

tag-output.comment: {{ expr }} — an output tag; expr is a JS expression whose value is stringified into the rendered markdown.
tag-output.name: meta.embedded.line.mdy

tag-code.comment: {% ... %} — a code tag; contents are raw JS statements (control flow, declarations, $.emit/$.render calls) spliced directly into the compiled template function. Braces need not balance within a single tag (a { for/if } is often opened in one tag and closed in a later one).
tag-code.name: meta.embedded.line.mdy

patterns.comment: $ is the template's native-function namespace ($.find, $.render, $.emit, $.resize, $.tokenize, $.rfc822, $.markdown, plus any embedder-supplied natives) — highlighted like a language-provided variable (e.g. `this`), not a plain identifier.
patterns.name: variable.language.dollar.mdy
